name: Ouroboros Executive Division Poplin
description:
The standard dress shirt issued to Ouroboros Corponation's mid-to-upper management tier, cut from a wrinkle-resistant poplin weave that maintains its crispness through a fourteen-hour shift without ironing. The collar is a semi-spread construction with collar stays sewn directly into the fabric — they cannot be removed. French placket, mitered cuffs, a subtle geometric pattern woven into the white-on-white fabric that's only visible at certain angles of light. The Ouroboros serpent logo appears in embossed thread on the left cuff, small and tasteful.

The shirt comes in three colorways — white, pale grey, and a blue-grey that Ouroboros internal documentation calls 'Meridian Blue.' There is no off-the-rack version of this shirt; it is issued, not purchased, and the issuance is tracked. Wearing one outside of Ouroboros facilities without authorization is technically a breach of employment contract. Most people don't know that. The shirt fits well because Ouroboros took body scans during onboarding.
what_it_says: You work for Ouroboros, and you are in a position where Ouroboros has decided you should look like it. Whether that's a point of pride or a collar depends entirely on how you feel about your employer.
worn_by: anyone trying to pass as Ouroboros personnel
story_hooks: The collar stays in the shirt contain a passive RFID chip that logs the wearer's location whenever they pass an Ouroboros sensor node — the company maps its employees' movements more precisely than anyone realizes.

A character acquires one of these shirts and uses it to bluff their way into an Ouroboros facility, only to discover that the shirt itself broadcasts a low-level ID signal that the building's security reads on entry.

An Ouroboros mid-manager keeps wearing their issued shirt after being quietly let go — technically illegal, but they haven't been approached yet, and they're not sure if that's because nobody noticed or because someone is watching to see what they do next.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A precisely tailored corporate dress shirt with an air of understated authority. The semi-spread collar sits with architectural precision, and the overall silhouette reads sharp and confident—the kind of garment that commands respect in boardrooms and automated meeting spaces. The white-on-white geometric pattern gives it subtle depth when light catches it at certain angles, suggesting hidden sophistication.
physical_description.fit: Tailored to individual body scans during onboarding—perfectly contoured through the shoulders and torso. Not loose, not restrictive. A second skin of corporate conformity. Mitered cuffs sit cleanly at the wrist, neither billowing nor constraining.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade wrinkle-resistant poplin weave—synthetic blend optimized for durability and minimal maintenance. The fabric maintains its structure through extended wear without degradation or creasing.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and crisp to the touch, with a subtle weave pattern visible only under direct light. The embossed thread of the Ouroboros logo adds minimal tactile interest on the left cuff. The collar stays, sewn directly into the fabric, create subtle reinforced ridges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Three sanctioned colorways: bright white (standard), pale grey (alternative), and Meridian Blue (official designation). All feature the woven geometric pattern in matching tones, creating a tonal-on-tonal effect that reads as refined restraint.
physical_description.closures: French placket front with concealed button closures. Buttons appear matte and corporate-neutral. Mitered cuffs button with dual-button construction for executive presentation.
distinctive_features: Non-removable collar stays sewn directly into fabric—physical embodiment of corporate permanence
Embossed Ouroboros serpent logo on left cuff (small, understated, traceable)
Woven white-on-white geometric pattern visible only at oblique angles—Easter egg for those who know
Custom tailoring based on individual body scans—no two fit identically
Serial tracking system tied to employment contract—issuance is documented and monitored
French placket and mitered cuffs suggest bespoke tailoring, though mass-produced for tier-appropriate personnel
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury and control. This is not aspirational wear—it is issued to mid-to-upper management as a uniform of privilege. Owning one without authorization marks you as either employed by Ouroboros or in possession of stolen corpo property.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals alignment with Ouroboros Corporation's vertical hierarchy and values. It is a visible contract in fabric form. Outside corporate facilities, it reads as either current employment, recent severance, or theft. The shirt exists in a liminal space—formal enough for any professional setting, but marked enough that informed observers know exactly where your loyalty (or lack thereof) lies.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine. The wrinkle-resistant poplin and corporate maintenance standards ensure these shirts are kept in showroom condition. Even after fourteen-hour shifts, they emerge unwrinkled and ready for the next cycle. Signs of wear are minimal unless deliberately abused—which would itself be a violation.

Semi-spread collar perfectly positioned, Meridian Blue or white colorway catching moody sidelight that reveals the subtle woven geometric pattern. Soft spotlight on the left cuff highlighting the embossed Ouroboros serpent logo. Background: sleek corporate office interior or rain-slicked rooftop overlooking GLMZ skyline at dusk.
